Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Expectation2: Perform maintenance and cleaning of the machines to ensure optimal performance
Situation2: Routine servicing is scheduled next week during a planned shutdown.
Story: I was halfway through my lunch break when my phone buzzed. It was Sam, my oldest friend, his voice tight with panic. “I think I left my passport at home. Can you check and bring it to the airport? My flight’s in two hours.” I could hear the desperation in his voice, and I knew how much this trip meant to him. As a friend, I wanted to drop everything and help. But I was also the only machine repairer on duty, and today was the only window before next week’s shutdown to prep the machines for maintenance. My supervisor had stressed how crucial it was to get everything ready—any delay could mean hours of lost production. I stared at the clock, feeling the weight of both roles pressing down on me. If I left now, I’d let down my team and risk the machines not being ready. If I stayed, I’d be letting down Sam when he needed me most. My mind raced, torn between loyalty to my friend and responsibility to my job, the pressure building as I tried to figure out what to do.
